title: Cousin Henry's funeral and sudden death
summary: Big funeral with bands; she recounts the news that Henry died, apparently from poisoned whiskey.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Do you remember Henry's, you know, his funeral? His who? His funeral. Oh, yeah. I was in that funeral.

They say that was one of the, uh, places the city ever had. That's right. You know it was large. You know where the St. Mary's Cemetery is. I can't place that now. I suspect Hickory. Hickory and Lowell Eye. I know where that is. Well, one part of the people was getting out there and the other part was still getting in at the house. And the house was at, um, Hickory and Hickory. Right on the corner. The corner house was at Hickory.
Is it Cross-Carrot? I mean, uh, St. Charles. Cross St. Charles. I know exactly where Hickory is. Uh-huh. Yeah, I've been up in that neighborhood. There's plenty of-
Well, they had, uh, two bands. Two bands or three bands. Anyhow, I believe Happy was toting his drum. They had it all draped with crepe. We wasn't playing it at all.
Which Happy was that? Little Happy. The one that's alive now? Uh-huh. He was on the taxi call. Plays with the Eureka bands. Yeah, I don't know where Happy lived, but I knew it was him.

Not red Happy? Uh-uh. Not red. A dark one. Yeah, there's two of the Happys that always get to- No, I don't mean red. I mean the dark one. So Happy carried him as he knows? Uh-huh. Well, I'll be. That must have been a big one. It was a funeral, I'm telling you. Everybody talked about that funeral. How many bands did that have? I think they had two or three if I'm mistaken. Because it happened so quick. I just left the boy the day before. He played a funeral out, St. Mary, and Chippewa. And he said, we got another one to play tomorrow. He said, in Carlton. I said, yeah. He said, don't you come and bring that child. He said, that's too much of walking. I said, I'll be there. I used to follow the band everywhere they went. So, uh, I went on home and I was washing. After he knocked off, he come by there and they bought me some beer and we talked. He said, I see you tomorrow. And I said, yeah. He said, don't bring the baby. I said, uh-uh. Me and her like to dance. That was my little niece I had. A little bit of thing like that and come in here just now. So we was home there the next morning. I said, well, let me hurry up. I said, because that funeral of them called them for one o'clock. I don't wash them so well. Well, I just remember who it was coming there and say, is your name this place? I said, yeah. I said, I want to take the corner grocery on the phone. I went to the corner and I answered. And his sister said to me, say, Bernice? I said, yeah. I said, Henry just died. I said, what Henry? I thought you were going to tell me my uncle had died. His daddy, you know.
She said, little Henry. I said, what? She said, he just died there.

Well, I got back there one night. It was a client in Magnolia. They had this little place, restaurant. I got back there. I seen so many people. I seen the police. I said, my God, it's true. So I went on up in there and he was looking. Couldn't get him to the hospital because he died right there. I said, somebody had given him some poison whiskey. I don't know what to say. The woman, what he had, had given it to him. He was going to marry. Well, he had been punished the house out for the girl. He had done what? Punished the house for a young girl and had everything in it. He was going to leave out the house with this woman and marry her. He wasn't married to that woman. They just came with her. And they said something the fellow in the band told him.
We never did find out who did it though. Well, times were really bad then about that.
Yeah. Everybody was upset. He died down like anything else.
